title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases of Judicial Review of Arbitration

articles.content_en:
Article 2 A case for applying for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court or a special people's court of the place where the arbitration institution agreed upon in the arbitration agreement is located, the place where the arbitration agreement is signed, the domicile of the applicant, or the domicile of the respondent.
Where a case concerns the validity of an arbitration agreement for a maritime or shipping dispute, it shall be under the jurisdiction of a maritime court of the place where the arbitration institution agreed upon in the arbitration agreement is located, the place where the arbitration agreement is signed, the domicile of the applicant, or the domicile of the respondent; if there is no maritime court in the aforesaid places, it shall be under the jurisdiction of the nearest maritime court.

Article 3 Where a foreign arbitral award is related to a case being tried by a People's Court, and neither the domicile of the respondent nor the location of the respondent's property is within the mainland of China, if the applicant applies for recognition of the foreign arbitral award, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court that accepts the related case. If the People's Court accepting the related case is a Primary People's Court, the case for applying for recognition of the foreign arbitral award shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the next higher level above that Primary People's Court. If the People's Court accepting the related case is a Higher People's Court or the Supreme People's Court, the said court shall decide whether to conduct the review itself or to designate an Intermediate People's Court to conduct the review.
Where a foreign arbitral award is related to a case being tried by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China, and neither the domicile of the respondent nor the location of the respondent's property is within the mainland of China, if the applicant applies for recognition of the foreign arbitral award, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the arbitration institution that accepts the related case is located.
Article 4 Where an applicant files an application with two or more People's Courts that have jurisdiction, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court that first dockets the case.

Article 7 Where the documents submitted by an applicant do not comply with the provisions of Article 5 or Article 6, and after the People's Court provides clarification, the submitted documents still fail to comply with the provisions, the People's Court shall make a ruling not to accept the case.
Where an applicant files an application with a People's Court that does not have jurisdiction over the case, the People's Court shall inform it to file the application with a People's Court that does have jurisdiction; if the applicant still does not change the application, the People's Court shall make a ruling not to accept the case.
If an applicant is dissatisfied with the ruling not to accept the case, it may file an appeal.

Article 8 Where a People's Court, after docketing a case, discovers that the case does not meet the conditions for acceptance, it shall make a ruling to dismiss the application.
For a case in which the application is dismissed by a ruling as provided in the preceding paragraph, if the applicant applies again and the application meets the conditions for acceptance, the People's Court shall accept the case.
If a party is dissatisfied with the ruling to dismiss the application, it may file an appeal.

Article 9 A People's Court shall, within seven days, examine and decide whether to accept an application filed by an applicant.
After accepting an arbitration judicial review case, the People's Court shall, within five days, issue a notice to the applicant and the respondent, informing them of the acceptance and the relevant rights and obligations.

Article 10 After a People's Court accepts an arbitration judicial review case, if the respondent raises an objection to the jurisdiction, it shall do so within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice from the People's Court. The People's Court shall examine the objection raised by the respondent and make a ruling thereon. If a party is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may file an appeal.
If a respondent that does not have a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China raises an objection to the jurisdiction of the People's Court, it shall do so within thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice from the People's Court.
Article 11 When a People's Court reviews an arbitration judicial review case, it shall form a collegial panel and question the parties.

Article 12 An arbitration agreement or an arbitral award that falls under the circumstances provided for in Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations (I) shall be a foreign-related arbitration agreement or a foreign-related arbitral award.

Article 13 Where the parties agree to choose the law applicable to the confirmation of the validity of a foreign-related arbitration agreement, they shall make an express manifestation of intent. An agreement only on the law applicable to the contract shall not be taken as the law applicable to the confirmation of the validity of the arbitration clause in the contract.

Article 14 Where a People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, determines the law applicable to the confirmation of the validity of a foreign-related arbitration agreement, if the parties have not chosen the applicable law, and the application of the law of the place where the arbitration institution is located and the application of the law of the place of arbitration would lead to different determinations on the validity of the arbitration agreement, the People's Court shall apply the law under which the arbitration agreement is confirmed as valid.

Article 15 Where an arbitration agreement does not specify the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration, but the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration can be determined in accordance with the arbitration rules agreed to be applicable in the arbitration agreement, the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration shall be deemed as the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration provided for in Article 18 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations.

Article 16 Where a People's Court applies the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards to review a case where a party applies for recognition and enforcement of a foreign arbitral award, if the respondent challenges the validity of the arbitration agreement as a defense, the People's Court shall, in accordance with Article V(1)(a) of the said Convention, determine the law applicable to the confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement.

Article 17 A People's Court's review of a case for applying for enforcement of a non-foreign-related arbitral award made by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China shall be governed by the provisions of Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
A People's Court's review of a case for applying for enforcement of a foreign-related arbitral award made by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China shall be governed by the provisions of Article 274 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 18 The acts of an arbitrator, when arbitrating the case, of soliciting or accepting bribes, engaging in malpractice for personal gain, or making an award perverting the law as provided for in Article 58(1)(6) of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 237(2)(6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China refer to such acts that have been confirmed by an effective criminal legal document or a disciplinary sanction decision.

Article 19 After a People's Court accepts an arbitration judicial review case but before it makes a ruling, if the applicant requests to withdraw the application, the People's Court shall make a ruling to permit the withdrawal.

Article 20 A ruling made by a People's Court in an arbitration judicial review case, except for a ruling on non-acceptance, dismissal of the application, or objection to jurisdiction, shall become legally effective upon service. If a party applies for reconsideration, files an appeal, or applies for retrial, the People's Court shall not accept it, unless otherwise provided by laws or judicial interpretations.

Article 21 A case accepted by a People's Court for applying for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement involving the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, or the Taiwan Region, or a case for applying for enforcement or setting aside of an arbitral award made by an arbitration institution in the mainland of China that involves the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, or the Taiwan Region, shall be reviewed by reference to the provisions on the judicial review of foreign-related arbitration cases.

Article 22 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2018. Where any judicial interpretations previously issued by this Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
